carried-beside-a-clan-tag: Carried beside a clan tag. A rank crest is a place in a competition: the number on it is that place, its colour says which board. Ratings earn none, because being high on WN8 is not something a clan wins.

clan-board.name: {board}, top {rank}
clan-board.how: A place in the top {rank} of the {board}. Held while the clan holds the place, and lost when it does not.

clan-overflow: A clan holding more than three places folds the rest into a {plus} crest, best first, so the tag stays readable. Hovering it names them.

featured-tournament-winner.name: Featured tournament winner
featured-tournament-winner.how: The same, won at an event Wargaming flags as featured. Gold instead of steel, exactly as on the player side.

heading: Every {badge} and how to earn it
marks-carried-beside-a-nickname: Marks carried beside a nickname wherever it appears on {NAME}: leaderboards, clan rosters, search, tournament brackets.

onslaught-champion.name: Onslaught Champion
onslaught-champion.how: Reached the Champion rank in Onslaught, which is what it takes to appear on the {standings} at all. Kept afterwards: a rating that falls back below the bar takes the place, not the fact that it was held.

onslaught-legend.name: Onslaught Legend
onslaught-legend.how: Held a place inside the season’s Legend cutoff, which is a position rather than a score: only so many exist at once, and the bar is judged against the season it was held in. Violet instead of steel blue, the colour the standings themselves paint Legend.

player-overflow: A player carrying more than three folds the rest into a {plus} crest, in the order above, so a nickname stays readable in a table. Hovering it names them, and each one still links where its own crest did.

streamer.name: Streamer
streamer.how: A Twitch channel linked to the account. Connect Twitch on your own profile to confirm it, and the crest links to your channel. It shows whether or not you are live.

streamer-who-is-on-air: A streamer who is on air also carries a red LIVE pill. That one is not earned and not kept: it appears when the stream starts and goes when it ends, so it is never folded away.
supporter-note: An active {link}, kept public. Supporters who choose to stay anonymous carry no badge, by their own choice.
the-marks-a-player-or: The marks a player or a clan can carry on {NAME}, what each one says, and exactly what it takes to get it.

tournament-winner.name: Tournament winner
tournament-winner.how: A team attributed to the clan won a tournament. Wargaming records teams and accounts, never clans, so the attribution is recovered by matching each roster against clan membership as it stood on the day it was played.

verified.name: Verified
verified.how: The owner has signed in with their Wargaming.net ID and connected this account. Signing in is the whole requirement, and it costs nothing.
